notes:
Both retrieved titles match the supplied references. Replication source is the published 2023 full manuscript deposited in the supplied OSF project (the input cites the 2022 OSF reference). Original text OCR corrupts N and η²; printed values retained without recalculation. Replication narrative and Table 9 agree on F=5.02, p=.025, partial eta-squared=0.01; supplementary Table S18 instead prints F=4.42 alongside the same p/effect size. Main-text target used. Replication full-sample N=860 is documented, but exact target analytic n is left null because the printed target residual df=855 is not reconciled and no separate test-specific n is printed. No metrics converted.
Completion source review (pval_value_o): Printed p < .05 belongs to the Study 1 numeracy-by-frame interaction, F(l, 96) = 5.6, matching the target relationship between numeracy and susceptibility to framing.
Completion source review (n_r): Final sample is explicitly 860 participants; the four studies were run together, and the Results introduction explicitly uses the full sample without subsequent exclusions. Initial screening removed 59 of 919 recruits. This is not inferred from degrees of freedom or a recruitment total alone.
Completion source review (es_value_r): The p. 11 Study 1 dichotomized-numeracy-by-framing interaction explicitly prints partial eta-squared 0.01; Table 9 corroborates the metric and value. Main-report F=5.02, p=.025 retained; supplementary Table S18 conflicts on F (4.42). No conversion performed.
Completion source review (reported_success): Authors explicitly conclude support for the Study 1 hypothesis, with weaker effects; coded successful from that target-specific narrative.
